# Adapt WebView controller contracts and ownership, not just package URLs

## Platform difference

OH-capable WebView packages can expose a different controller/event API and native lifetime than an application's previous backend.

## Implementation

Kazumi replaces its OH webview_flutter path with in-app WebView controllers, handlers and user scripts. Its later parsing overlay waits for initialization and survives independently of the video page, with subscription/disposal cleanup. NJU rewrites its old widget API to controller/widget separation and navigation delegates. Kazumi subsequently routes OH resolution callbacks through the shared notifier after upstream behavior changes.

## Applicability

Preserve application-specific parsing/login/notification contracts during backend replacement. A parser overlay solving off-page URL resolution is not a background download service.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

A plugin source swap alone may compile while missing navigation callbacks, cookies or JavaScript results. Recreating a native view for every route change can invalidate in-flight work.

## Verification

Test initialization ordering, JS handlers, navigation/error callbacks, source resolution after leaving the player page and disposal with outstanding callbacks.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
